question: What exact event marks the beginning of the third stage of labor?
explanation: The third stage starts right after the newborn is fully born and ends when the placenta is delivered. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is the immediate postpartum period considered a dangerous time for the mother?

options.A: The open placental site can bleed heavily
options.B: The cervix suddenly swells up with fluid
options.C: The pelvic bones separate to release pressure
options.D: The maternal blood pressure rises too fast

explanation: When the placenta detaches, it leaves open blood vessels that rely on strong uterine contractions to close off and stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of performing AMTSL on a postpartum mother?

options.B: To encourage early breast milk letdown
options.C: To test the placenta for infections

explanation: AMTSL is specifically bundled together to cut down the amount of blood lost after delivery and stop heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does active management differ from the natural delivery of the placenta?

options.A: Natural delivery relies heavily on high doses of intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Active management requires surgical removal of the placenta every time
options.C: Natural delivery takes less than two minutes to complete safely
options.D: Active management uses medications and traction to speed up separation

explanation: Instead of waiting for nature to take its course, the midwife intervenes promptly with uterotonics and controlled cord traction to control bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h2)

question: Within what timeframe should the uterotonic drug be given after the baby is born?

options.D: Only after the placenta comes out

explanation: Giving the uterotonic quickly is essential to stimulate the uterine muscle fibers before significant bleeding can occur. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following conditions makes ergometrine a dangerous choice for managing the third stage?
explanation: Ergometrine constricts blood vessels throughout the body, which can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure for hypertensive women. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h3)

question: What dangerous complication can happen if you pull on the umbilical cord without pushing the uterus upward?
explanation: Pulling the cord without providing counter-pressure to hold the uterus in place can pull the organ inside out. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h4)

question: When is the correct time to apply gentle traction to the umbilical cord during AMTSL?

options.A: When the uterus feels contracted and hard
options.B: Only after the placenta drops out on its own
options.C: Immediately as the baby's head crowns
options.D: While the mother is pushing out the infant

explanation: You must wait for a uterine contraction and palpable firmness before pulling, to ensure the placenta has separated safely. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of massaging the uterus right after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.B: To push out remaining amniotic fluid
options.C: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin
options.D: To keep the uterine muscle contracted

explanation: Massaging stimulates the myometrium to stay firmly clamped down so that bleeding is controlled. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h5)

question: How often should a midwife check the tone of the uterus during the first two hours postpartum?

options.A: Only if the mother complains of pain
options.B: Once before the mother leaves the labor ward

explanation: Frequent checks in the immediate postpartum window help catch early uterine relaxation before heavy blood loss occurs. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h5)

question: At what point is a placenta considered retained if it has not yet delivered?
explanation: If the placenta fails to deliver within thirty minutes despite active management, it is classified as a retained placenta requiring medical action. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to inspect the delivered placenta and membranes thoroughly?

options.A: To ensure no tissue was left inside the uterus
options.B: To measure the exact birth weight of the baby
options.C: To check if the umbilical cord was knotted
options.D: To prepare the tissue for laboratory testing

explanation: Missing a small piece of the placenta can cause persistent bleeding and postpartum infection later on. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h6)
